Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and pointers below; we can expand during the tech deep dive.

- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report. We can provide a redacted copy immediately; full report available under NDA. Redacted copy attached (SOC2_TypeII_Redacted.pdf).

- Encryption in transit & at rest: All customer traffic to our hosted API is TLS 1.2+; we enforce strong ciphers and mTLS for Dedicated/Private deployments if requested. Data at rest in our hosted environment is encrypted using AES-256.

- Customer-managed keys / BYOK:
  * Hosted: We support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For HSM-backed keys, we support AWS CloudHSM-backed keys through KMS customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs) and can accept HSM-wrapped key material in some Private deployments.
  * Dedicated/Private: For customers using Dedicated pools or Private deployment, you can bring your own KMS (connect to your KMS over a private link) or provide HSMs in your VPC.
  * Keys per tenant: We support per-customer key separation and can scope key usage by environment or workload.
  * Rotation & lifecycle: Rotation is customer-driven for BYOK; Redwood can automate rewrapping/rotation workflows on behalf of the customer with agreed SLAs.

- Logging & retention: By default we collect request metadata for observability; persistent request/response logging that contains PII can be disabled per-route. We also support customer-controlled retention windows and can implement 'no-logging' modes for sensitive workloads.

Attachments: KMS_FactSheet.pdf (details on KMS integrations and HSM support)

I'll be on the deep dive call and can bring a short architecture slide. Camila — can you propose Wed/Thu slots? Rishi can cover the integration patterns.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding a few technical specifics to help the security team triage before the call:

- In-transit: We use TLS 1.2/1.3; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can enable mutual TLS with client certs and enforce IP allowlists.

- At-rest: Data stored by Redwood is encrypted with AES-256. For Hosted with BYOK, the envelope encryption model uses your CMK to protect data keys; Redwood does not hold plaintext customer keys.

- KMS/HSM integration options:
  1) Hosted BYOK via cloud KMS: Redwood integrates with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) using IAM-based access to perform Encrypt/Decrypt operations. For HSM-backed keys, KMS provides an HSM root — customer CMKs can be configured to be HSM-backed.
  2) Private/Dedicated with private KMS: You can deploy a KMS in your VPC (e.g., Vault with HSM or in-cloud KMS) and connect via PrivateLink/VPN. We provide a connector pattern that keeps key operations local to your network when required.
  3) HSM-wrapped key import: For highly regulated environments, we support importing key material wrapped by an HSM; details vary by cloud and require an architecture review.

- Key usage & audit: We emit key usage events to audit logs and can forward those to your SIEM. Key access is logged and can be included in compliance packages.

- Doc/Artifacts to review: I'll bring a short integration diagram to the deep dive. If you can share the vendor security questionnaire (or a link to the form), we can start filling it out ahead of the meeting.

Thanks,
